title: People's Democratic Republic of Yemen
capsule: The People's Democratic Republic of Yemen — South Yemen — was proclaimed on 30 November 1967 when the National Liberation Front expelled the British from Aden and the former Aden Protectorate, becoming the Arab world's only avowedly Marxist state. The PDRY was governed successively by Presidents Qahtan al-Shaabi, Salim Rubai Ali (executed in the bloody 1978 intra-party coup), and Ali Nasir Muhammad, whose 1986 bid to consolidate power triggered a week-long civil war in Aden that killed thousands and forced his exile. The state maintained close ties with the Soviet Union and hosted Palestinian and German Red Army Faction militants. On 22 May 1990 the PDRY merged with the Yemen Arab Republic to form the unified Republic of Yemen, with Ali Abdullah Saleh of North Yemen as first president.
